item.content:encoded:
The layoffs are across its Singapore, Malaysia and Hong Kong offices

IHH Healthcare will see close to 400 employees leave as it moves to consolidate its business support services, The Business Times reported.

The healthcare group said in a statement on Thursday (Nov 4) that those affected are from its Singapore, Hong Kong and Malaysia offices.

In Singapore, IHH’s brands include Parkway, Gleneagles and Mount Elizabeth. Across 10 countries, including Malaysia and India, the group runs 190 healthcare facilities, and 89 of them are hospitals.

item.content:encoded:
[This is a sponsored article with Malaysian Research Accelerator for Technology and Innovation (MRANTI).]

Malaysian technology companies will soon be able to bring our innovations to international markets, specifically Central Asia, thanks to a new partnership with Kazakhstan. 

This was formalised just yesterday (November 4, 2026) through a tripartite Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) with Malaysian Research Accelerator for Technology and Innovation (MRANTI), the Malaysia Smart Cities Alliance Association (MSCA) and the Alatau City Authority Special Management Organization (SMO), this will open doors for local firms to test technologies, explore market opportunities, and commercialise solutions in Kazakhstan.

item.content:encoded:
Disclaimer: Unless otherwise stated, any opinions expressed below belong solely to the author. List published by the Ministry of Manpower.

Singapore’s economy may be growing at a record pace this year, but the boom—driven by demand for AI-related hardware products—has had an uneven impact on the job market.

The total number of unemployed citizens increased to 64,700 last quarter, the highest figure since 2021. It was driven by a relatively high number of redundancies (4,800)—and the last time more Singaporeans were laid off in a single quarter was in Q4 of 2020, when it hit 5,640.

item.content:encoded:
Revenue still fell 18% as the group shrank its footprint

Japan Foods has returned to profit after closing nearly a third of its Singapore outlets and shifting its focus to halal dining concepts and affordable meals, The Business Times reported.

The Singapore-listed group operates Japanese-cuisine brands, including Ajisen Ramen and Yakiniku Shokudo—and has been in the red since 2023.

item.content:encoded:
This year is its best in five years, says founder and CEO Dean Ahmad

Amid a spate of gym closures, UFIT is bucking the trend.

According to its CEO and founder, Dean Ahmad, 41, the homegrown health and fitness brand has generated between S$15-S$18 million in annual revenue every year since 2023, growing by almost 10% year-on-year.

This year, he said, is its best in five years—and its most profitable.

But how is it raking in multi-million-dollar revenues with just four outlets in Singapore? Vulcan Post spoke with Dean to find out.

Selling outcomes

item.content:encoded:
Zermatt Neo’s restaurant is giving out meals for free if you can finish its food challenges

8kg. 9kg. 10kg. For local competitive eater Zermatt Neo, 38, that is a normal amount of food to finish in one sitting—and it is also why people keep watching his videos.

But you don’t have to eat like Zermatt to dine at his new restaurant.

Opening today (30 Oct), Over serves local comfort food in portions ranging from individual meals to large sharing platters. Diners who are feeling particularly adventurous can also turn any dish into a food challenge.

Vulcan Post spoke with Zermatt to find out more about his new venture, what diners can expect, and whether he has plans to take Over beyond its first outlet.

item.content:encoded:
Resident unemployment has climbed to 3%

Retrenchments rose by 3.9% to 4,800 in Q3 2026, up from 4,620 in Q2, according to the latest Ministry of Manpower (MOM)’s Labour Market Advance Release on Friday (Oct 30).

Retrenchments in Q3 2026 are the ​highest since the 5,640 layoffs recorded in Q4 2020. The incidence of retrenchment held constant at 2.0 for every 1,000 employees.

MOM said business reorganisation continued to be the main driver of retrenchments

This would’ve been fine, if I had not also accidentally broken my only pair of glasses from a treadmill incident (yes, it was very embarrassing). So as is expected of someone with […]
item.content:encoded:
A couple months ago, I made the mistake of scratching my eyeball, which meant I couldn’t wear my contact lenses while it healed.

This would’ve been fine, if I had not also accidentally broken my only pair of glasses from a treadmill incident (yes, it was very embarrassing).

So as is expected of someone with over -400 and -500 vision, I panicked. It was mid-month and prescription glasses are expensive, especially with the additional frills that I need, like lens features for astigmatism and anti-blue light. I can’t be going to work “blind.”

Then my guardian angel (Claudia) introduced me to 100glasses, a new Malaysian online optical store that sells affordable prescription glasses made in Johor from as low as RM49, and my life was saved.

Disclaimer: Unless otherwise stated, any opinions expressed below belong solely to the author. Data sourced from the latest official release by HDB.

HDB resale prices are continuing their gradual decline, with the Resale Price Index dipping marginally by 0.1% for the third consecutive quarter, the first time since 2014.

However, this is just an overall average. To get a clearer picture of the market, it makes more sense to look at town-level data, which captures resale transactions completed over the past quarter.

Following the particularly severe haze episode in 2015, when skies over much of Southeast Asia were blanketed in smoke for many days between Jun and Oct, researchers at Harvard attempted to estimate the impact of the extraordinarily polluted air on health and mortality.

After all, haze is treated mostly as an inconvenience, and few people believe it could kill them — but there is a real damage that it causes to millions exposed to it.
